holidays.name: National Chicken Wing Day
holidays.description: A saucy, finger-licking salute to the humble wing. Fans mark it with piles of drumettes and flats, bowls of blue cheese or ranch, and a stack of napkins. Mild, hot, honey garlic and lemon pepper all count.
holidays.origin: The tradition traces back to Buffalo, New York. In 1977 the city issued a proclamation honoring Anchor Bar co-owner Frank Bellissimo and declared July 29 Chicken Wing Day. The Anchor Bar is widely credited with popularizing the Buffalo wing.
holidays.funFact: Wings began as a bar snack in Buffalo. They are now a national obsession, and the holiday itself was launched by a city proclamation.

holidays.name: National Lasagna Day
holidays.description: A celebration of layered noodles, rich sauce and gooey melted cheese. Bake a classic meat lasagna, try a veggie or white-sauce version, or make one for a neighbor.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that has become a fixture of the summer food-day calendar. It honors one of Italy's best-known comfort dishes.
holidays.funFact: The community kindness group Lasagna Love uses the day to spotlight its volunteers. They have delivered hundreds of thousands of homemade meals to neighbors.
